title: Matzo Ball Soup
description: Classic Jewish comfort food featuring light and fluffy matzo balls simmered in a savory broth.
author: Unknown

ingredients.note: rendered chicken fat, coconut oil or vegetable oil

instructions: Finely chop the parsley and grate the ginger.
In a large bowl, combine the eggs, schmaltz, stock, matzo meal, nutmeg, ginger and parsley.
Season with 1 teaspoon salt and a few grinds of pepper. Gently mix with a whisk or spoon.
Cover and refrigerate until chilled, about 3 hours or overnight.
Fill a wide, deep pan with lightly salted water and bring to a boil.
With wet hands, take some of the mix and mold it into the size and shape of a Ping-Pong ball.
Gently drop it into the boiling water, repeating until all the mix is used.
Cover the pan, reduce heat to a lively simmer and cook matzo balls about 30 to 40 minutes.
tips: If desired, the cooked matzo balls can be transferred to chicken or vegetable soup and served immediately.
Alternatively, they may be placed on a baking sheet and frozen, then transferred to a freezer bag and kept frozen until a few hours before serving; reheat in chicken or vegetable soup or broth.

title: Homemade Chicken Noodle Soup
description: A comforting soup with homemade egg noodles, tender chicken, and vegetables.
author: Unknown
instructions: For the noodles, beat the egg and soften the butter. For the soup, chop the onion and celery, slice the carrots, mince the garlic, and shred the chicken.
To prepare the homemade noodles, stir together flour and salt in a large bowl.
Add the beaten egg, milk, and softened butter.
Knead dough until smooth, about 5 minutes, then let it rest in a covered bowl for 10 minutes.
On a floured surface, roll the dough out to 1/8 or 1/4 inch thickness.
Cut into desired lengths and shapes, then separate and allow to air dry.
For the soup, in a large pot over medium heat, melt 2 tablespoons of butter.
Cook onion, celery, and carrots in butter until just tender, about 5 minutes.
Add the garlic and cook for an additional minute.
Pour in chicken broth and stir in the noodles, basil, oregano, poultry seasoning (if using), salt, and pepper.
Bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer for about 15-20 minutes.
Stir in the shredded chicken and cook until heated through, then serve.
tips: For best results with homemade noodles, let them air dry for a couple of hours. If in a rush, 30 minutes will work.
Serve with peanuts, sriracha, and green onion for topping if desired.

title: Chickpea Curry
description: A simple and flavorful vegan curry made with chickpeas in a rich coconut-tomato sauce.
author: Unknown
instructions: Slice the onion, mince the garlic, and chop the cilantro.
In a large pot, heat the oil over medium-low.
Add the sliced onion, garlic, and crushed red pepper.
Cook, stirring occasionally, until the onion is softened and deep golden, about 15 minutes.
Increase the heat to medium.
Add the curry powder and cumin and stir until toasted, about 1 minute.
Add the crushed tomatoes and scrape the bottom of the pan to release any browned bits.
Pour in the coconut milk and add the chickpeas.
Stir, reduce to low heat, and let simmer until the sauce is thickened, about 10 minutes.
Season with salt and pepper to taste.
Garnish with chopped cilantro and serve with lime wedges over rice or with naan.
tips: Add a tablespoon of water at a time if the onions get dry while cooking.

title: Spicy Mushroom Pasta
description: A quick pasta dish with a spicy tomato and mushroom sauce.
author: Unknown
instructions: Dice the garlic and bell peppers, and slice the mushrooms.
Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil and cook spaghetti according to package directions.
Meanwhile, heat olive oil and butter in a large skillet.
Add garlic and cook for one minute, stirring often.
Add Thai chilis and stir constantly for 10-15 seconds.
Add bell peppers and cook for 3 minutes.
Add mushrooms and cook for 7-10 minutes.
Stir in tomato paste, salt, pepper, and rosemary. Cook for 5 minutes, stirring often.
Reserve 1 cup of pasta water, then drain the spaghetti.
Add the reserved pasta water to the sauce and bring to a simmer.
Add the cooked spaghetti to the sauce, along with red pepper flakes and parmesan cheese.
Toss to combine and serve immediately.

title: Tomato Mushroom Sauce
description: A simple and quick vegetarian pasta sauce with tomatoes, mushrooms, and spinach.
author: Unknown
instructions: Dice the onion, bell pepper, and garlic. Slice the mushrooms and tear the spinach into small pieces.
In a medium pot, sauté the onion and bell pepper for one minute.
Add the garlic and cook for one more minute.
Add the spices and toast for 1-2 minutes.
Add the mushrooms and cook for 3-4 minutes.
Stir in the crushed tomatoes and spinach, and let the sauce simmer for 8-10 minutes.

title: Mushroom Sausage Strata
description: A savory breakfast casserole with sausage, mushrooms, and cheese, perfect for preparing overnight.
author: Unknown
instructions: Grease a 13x9-in. baking dish, cube the bread slices, and shred the cheeses.
In a large skillet, cook sausage over medium heat until no longer pink; drain.
Place the bread cubes in the prepared baking dish.
Sprinkle with the sausage, mushrooms and cheeses.
In a large bowl, whisk eggs, milk, cream, Worcestershire sauce and pepper; pour mixture over the cheese.
Cover the dish and refrigerate overnight.
Remove from the refrigerator 30 minutes before baking.
Preheat the oven to 350°.
Bake, uncovered, for 35-45 minutes or until a knife inserted near the center comes out clean.
tips: Freeze Option: After assembling, cover and freeze strata. To use, partially thaw in the refrigerator overnight. Remove from the refrigerator 30 minutes before baking. Preheat oven to 350° and bake as directed, increasing time as necessary.

title: Mushroom Beef
description: A hearty beef stew with a rich mushroom flavor, perfect served over egg noodles.
author: Unknown
instructions: Cube the beef roast, slice the mushrooms, chop the carrots and onion, and mince the garlic and rosemary.
Bring broth and dried mushrooms to a boil in a large saucepan. Remove from heat and let stand for 15-20 minutes until mushrooms are softened.
Drain mushrooms, reserving the liquid. Finely chop the mushrooms and set aside.
Combine flour, salt and pepper in a bag; set aside 1 tablespoon for the sauce.
Add beef to the remaining flour mixture and shake to coat.
In a Dutch oven, brown the beef in oil in batches.
Add portobello mushrooms, carrots and onion; saute until onion is tender.
Add garlic, rosemary and rehydrated mushrooms; cook for 1 minute.
Stir in the reserved flour mixture until blended, then gradually stir in the reserved mushroom broth.
Bring to a boil, then reduce heat, cover and simmer for 1.5-2 hours or until beef is tender.
Combine cornstarch and cold water until smooth, then gradually stir it into the pan.
Bring to a boil; cook and stir for 2 minutes or until thickened.
Serve the stew with egg noodles if desired and top with blue cheese.
tips: Freeze Option: Freeze stew in freezer containers for up to 6 months. To use, thaw overnight in the refrigerator and reheat in a Dutch oven.

title: Beef & Mushroom Braised Stew
description: A rich and savory beef stew braised with red wine, brandy, and herbs.
author: Unknown

ingredients.note: 1/4 tsp each of parsley, rosemary, sage, tarragon, thyme

instructions: Cut beef roast into 1-inch cubes, slice the mushrooms and onions, and mince the garlic.
Preheat the oven to 325°.
Sprinkle beef with salt and pepper.
In an ovenproof Dutch oven, heat oil over medium heat and brown the beef in batches.
Remove beef from the pan.
Add mushrooms and onions to the pan; cook and stir until tender.
Add garlic and cook 1 minute longer.
Stir in broth, wine, brandy, tomato paste and herbs.
Return beef to the pan and bring to a boil.
Bake, covered, for 1 hour.
In a small bowl, mix flour and water until smooth, then gradually stir into the stew.
Bake, covered, for 30 minutes longer or until stew is thickened and beef is tender.
Skim fat and serve the stew with mashed potatoes.
tips: Freeze Option: Freeze stew in freezer containers. To use, partially thaw in the refrigerator overnight. Heat through in a saucepan, stirring occasionally.

title: Chicken Tortilla Bake
description: A layered casserole with chicken, tortillas, and cheese, similar to an enchilada bake.
author: Unknown
instructions: Preheat oven to 350°. Grease a 13x9-in. baking dish. Shred the cooked chicken, finely chop the onion, shred the cheese, and warm the tortillas.
In a large bowl, combine the chicken, chilies, broth, soups and onion.
Layer half of the tortillas in the baking dish, cutting to fit if needed.
Top with half of the chicken mixture and half of the cheese.
Repeat the layers.
Bake, uncovered, for 30 minutes or until heated through.
tips: Freeze Option: Cover and freeze the unbaked casserole. To use, partially thaw overnight in the refrigerator. Let stand for 30 minutes before baking as directed, increasing time as necessary until a thermometer reads 165°.

title: Creamy Chicken Enchiladas
description: Rich and creamy chicken enchiladas made with a savory soup and cheese sauce.
author: Unknown

ingredients.item: diced tomatoes with green chilies canned

instructions: Preheat oven to 350°. Grease two 13x9-in. baking dishes. Remove chicken from bones and shred. Cube the cream cheese and warm the tortillas.
In a large bowl, combine tomatoes, soups, milk and seasonings.
Transfer 3.5 cups of the mixture to another bowl and stir in the chicken and cream cheese.
Spread 1/4 cup of the plain soup mixture into the bottom of each baking dish.
Place 1/2 cup of the chicken mixture down the center of each tortilla.
Roll up the tortillas and place them seam side down in the baking dishes.
Pour the remaining soup mixture over the enchiladas and sprinkle with cheese.
Bake, uncovered, for 30-35 minutes until heated through.
Broil for 1-2 minutes until golden brown.
tips: Freeze Option: Cover and freeze unbaked casseroles for up to 3 months. To use, partially thaw overnight in the refrigerator and let stand for 30 minutes before baking. Cover with foil and bake at 350° for 45 minutes or until 165°. Uncover and bake 5-10 minutes more until cheese is melted.

title: Apricot Bacon Pinwheels
description: Simple and elegant appetizers made with puff pastry, apricot preserves, cheese, and bacon.
author: Unknown
instructions: Preheat oven to 400° and line a baking sheet with parchment paper. Thaw the puff pastry, shred the cheese, and cook and crumble the bacon.
Unfold the pastry and layer with preserves, mustard, cheese and bacon.
Roll up jelly-roll style and cut into 16 slices.
Place cut side down on the prepared baking sheet.
Bake for 15-20 minutes or until golden brown.
tips: Freeze Option: Freeze cooled appetizers in a freezer bag. To use, reheat on a parchment-lined baking sheet in a 400° oven until crisp.

title: Frank's RedHot Buffalo Chicken Dip
description: The classic party dip featuring spicy buffalo sauce, chicken, and a creamy cheese blend.
author: Frank's RedHot
instructions: Shred the cooked chicken and soften the cream cheese.
Preheat oven to 350°F.
Mix all ingredients in a large bowl.
Spoon into a shallow 1-quart baking dish.
Bake for 20 minutes or until the mixture is heated through, then stir.
tips: Sprinkle with green onions and additional blue cheese if desired.
Serve with chips, crackers, and/or cut up veggies.

title: Wonton Soup
description: A quick and easy soup with frozen wontons in a savory ginger and soy-infused broth.
author: Unknown
instructions: Mince the fresh ginger, chop the cilantro, and roughly chop the cashews.
Add the chicken broth, soy sauce, rice vinegar, sesame oil, sweet chili sauce, and ginger to a medium-large pot over high heat.
Bring the mixture to a boil, stirring occasionally.
Add the wontons, frozen peas, and baby spinach.
Continue to cook over high heat for about 3 minutes until the wontons are warmed through.
Remove from heat and stir in cilantro.
Serve the soup garnished with chopped cashews.
tips: White vinegar can be used as a substitute for rice vinegar.

title: Creamy Tuscan Sausage Gnocchi
description: A one-pan meal featuring Italian sausage and potato gnocchi in a creamy sun-dried tomato and spinach sauce.
author: Unknown
instructions: Mince the garlic, grate the parmesan cheese, and remove sausage meat from its casings.
In a deep skillet, sauté the sausage over medium-high heat until browned, about 5-7 minutes.
Stir in the garlic and cook for about 30 seconds.
Add the chicken broth, cream, lemon juice, sun-dried tomatoes, and gnocchi to the pan and stir.
Reduce the heat to medium, cover, and cook for 5 minutes.
Stir the gnocchi and add the spinach.
Cover the pan again for 1-2 minutes until the spinach has wilted.
Stir in the parmesan and basil (if using).
Season with salt & pepper to taste and serve immediately.
tips: There is no need to pre-cook the gnocchi; it cooks in the sauce.
If using oil-packed sun-dried tomatoes, drain the oil before adding them to the skillet.

title: Sesame Chicken
description: A quick and easy stir-fry with sticky, sweet, and savory sesame sauce coating tender chicken.
author: Unknown
instructions: Cut chicken breasts into 1/2 inch cubes. Grate the ginger, mince the garlic, and chop the spring onions.
In a medium bowl, combine the soy sauce, honey, sriracha, ginger, garlic, sesame seeds and sesame oil for the sauce.
In a large bowl, combine the chicken, cornstarch, salt and pepper.
Heat a large pan over high heat for at least 2 minutes, then add oil and chicken.
Stir-fry the chicken for 5-6 minutes until golden brown.
Add the sauce and simmer for 3-4 minutes until it becomes thick and sticky.
Serve with hot white rice, sprinkled with chopped spring onions and more sesame seeds if desired.

title: Olive Garden Gnocchi Toscana Soup
description: A copycat recipe of the Olive Garden favorite, with chicken, sausage, gnocchi, and kale in a creamy broth.
author: Unknown
instructions: Dice the cooked chicken and white onion. Chop the celery and kale. Shred the carrots. Cut the potatoes into 1-inch pieces.
In a large pot, saute sausage for 5-6 minutes until browned. Transfer sausage to a plate using a slotted spoon.
In the same pot, melt the butter and saute celery, onions, and carrots for 2-3 minutes until onions are translucent.
Add garlic and saute for another minute until fragrant.
Add chicken, chicken broth, potatoes, thyme, salt, and pepper. Bring to a boil.
Boil until the potatoes are tender.
Gently add gnocchi and boil for 3-4 minutes longer, then reduce heat to a simmer.
Stir in the kale, heavy cream, and cooked sausage.
Taste and adjust seasoning if needed.
Serve garnished with grated parmesan cheese and/or bacon if desired.
